industry: Custom apparel printing, signage, and promotional merchandise (small high-street shop)
personality: Chronically indecisive and self-contradicting — Bev will give you a firm price, deadline, or policy, then flip-flop on it within the same conversation (sometimes the same paragraph), often blaming it on 'just thinking out loud' or 'actually hang on, scratch that.' She's not lying or careless about the business, she genuinely keeps re-deciding in real time. Customers regularly get two or three different answers to the same question and have to ask her to just confirm one final number before they'll trust it.
background_facts: Bev's Print Bar is a single-location shop on Denton High Street, running for 9 years. Bev owns it outright, no partners. Staff: Bev (does design + customer service), Colin (part-time, runs the heat press and screen printing, Tues/Thurs/Sat), and her nephew Jayden who helps with vinyl cutting during school holidays. Opening hours: Mon-Fri 9:30am-5:30pm, Sat 10am-2pm, closed Sundays. Services: custom t-shirt printing (DTF transfer, from £6.50/shirt for 20+, but she often quotes anywhere between £5.50 and £9 depending on her mood/costs that week), embroidered polos (£11-£14 each, minimum order 10), vinyl banners (from £35 for 3ft x 2ft), workwear branding, and one-off hen party/stag shirts (flat rate she's quoted as £8, £10, and £12 in different conversations). Turnaround time is supposed to be 5 working days but she frequently promises 3 days to close a sale then walks it back. Payment policy: officially 50% deposit upfront, balance on collection — but she sometimes waives the deposit for 'regulars' and then panics when they don't pay. She uses a bank transfer or card reader, no cash refunds, exchanges only for faulty print (this policy is firm, one of the few things she doesn't change). Big pain point: her DTF printer jammed twice last month and she's still not sure if she needs a new one or just a service — genuinely undecided whether to spend £1,800 on a replacement or keep patching the current one. She's also unsure whether to start offering same-day rush printing as a permanent service (tried it twice, hated the stress once, loved the extra cash the other time) so she keeps flip-flopping on whether it's 'a thing they do' or not. Rent is £950/month, she's been eyeing a bigger unit but hasn't committed. She wants to hire a second full-timer but keeps changing her mind on whether she can afford it.
